label: copy-phase re-input of digit 0 near the end of short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and essentially only when the fed-back input is the digit 0 (3900 of 3903 dev activations; it never fires on 0 in the original phase or at <DEL>). Activation is concentrated in short sequences (L=3-5, about 91% of mass) at the last 1-3 outputs (to_go <= 2). It is strongest when 0 was original token 1 of an L=4 sequence (step 6, recall_idx 2, prev2 = <DEL>; about 55% of mass). The top examples look like j 0 d 3 <DEL> j [0] d. It does not fire on other tokens or on 0 in long sequences except weakly. Precision is low (about 0.2): many matching contexts stay silent (e.g. x 0 t c, u 0 h u), so whether it fires seems to depend on the specific surrounding tokens in a way no simple variable captures. Being active only in the copy phase, it is not a generic 0 detector.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+6.13), orig4=- (+3.59), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+3.32), prev_tok=j (+2.96), orig6=3 (+2.88), phase=2 & out_tok=d (+2.77). Lower it: prev3_tok=0 (-3.02), to_go=6 (-2.52), L=4 & t=7 (-2.16), L=4 & recall_idx=3 (-2.16).
